brief:
Hamas, Islamic Jihad, and rival Fatah dissidents have formed an unprecedented coalition for Palestinian elections, the first ballot since 2006, Mondoweiss reported. The alignment represents a rare moment of unity among factions that have historically competed for political influence and control of Palestinian institutions.

The elections are taking place under conditions of Israeli military occupation and international diplomatic pressure, raising fundamental questions about whether genuinely free political competition can occur under foreign military rule. Observers have pointed to these structural constraints—Israeli security operations and external pressure from foreign governments—as potential impediments to meaningful democratic change, even as the unified opposition slate prepares to contest the ballot.
dek: Hamas, Islamic Jihad, and rival Fatah dissidents have united in an unprecedented coalition for the first Palestinian elections since 2006. But Israeli repression and foreign pressure raise doubts about whether free politics is possible under occupation.
title: Palestinians prepare first elections since 2006 amid occupation constraints
